chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The children of Ismail (peace be upon him) did not cease to be the governors of the House, and they established for the people their Hajj and the matters of their religion, inheriting it from an elder to an elder, until the time of Adnan ibn Uddad. So the term prolonged upon them, their hearts hardened, they became corrupt, and innovated in their religion, and expelled one another. Thus, from them were some who went out seeking livelihood, and from them were some who went out disliking fighting.

And in their hands were many things from the Hanifiyyah (uprightness), from the prohibition of mothers and daughters and whatever Allah prohibited in marriage, except that they permitted the wife of the father, and the daughter of the sister, and joining between two sisters.
And in their hands was the Hajj, and the Talbiyyah, and the Ghusl from the Janabah, except what they innovated in their Talbiyyah and in their Hajj from the Shirk (polytheism).
And between Ismail (peace be upon him) and Adnan ibn Uddad was Musa (peace be upon him).

key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: Sexual impurity requiring full ritual bath

ai.seo_question: What were the religious practices and innovations of the children of Ismail before the time of Adnan?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi traces the lineage of the Kaaba's custodianship from Ismail through Adnan, highlighting a period of stability before the Quraish's deviation from the pure monotheism (Hanifiyyah) of Ibrahim. It specifically notes the intergenerational transmission of ritual knowledge and the subsequent corruption of these rites through shirk and social innovations, such as polygamy and specific marriage prohibitions, setting the historical stage for the Prophet Muhammad's purification of the rites.
